memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: (The Israelites traveled from the wells of the Jaakanites to Moserah. There Aaron died and was buried, and Eleazar his son succeeded him as priest. From there they traveled to Gudgodah and on to Jotbathah, a land with streams of water. At that time the Lord set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the covenant of the Lord, to stand before the Lord to minister and to pronounce blessings in his name, as they still do today.) - Deut 10:6-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Tucked into this travel record is a significant note: God "set apart the tribe of Levi" for a special calling — to carry the ark, to minister before the Lord, and to pronounce blessings in His name. In a moving detail, the Levites received no share of land like the other tribes; instead, "the Lord is their inheritance" (v. 9). Their portion was not property but God Himself. To serve Him closely was their reward.

There is something beautiful in this. The Levites were called to a life of service and worship, and their compensation was the nearness of God. While others inherited fields and vineyards, the Levites inherited the privilege of standing before the Lord. This teaches us that the greatest treasure is not what we can accumulate but the God we get to know and serve. Nearness to God is worth more than any earthly portion.

Under the new covenant, this calling extends to all who belong to Christ. Peter tells believers that we are "a royal priesthood" (1 Pet 2:9) — every Christian is now set apart to worship, serve, and bless others in God's name. And like the Levites, our greatest inheritance is not earthly things but God Himself. The psalmist captured it: "You are my portion, Lord" (Ps 119:57). Whatever else you may or may not have in this life, if you have God, you have the greatest inheritance of all. Serve Him gladly, and treasure the nearness that is your true reward.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do I see nearness to God as my greatest treasure, or do I chase earthly portions?
- What does it mean that I am part of a "royal priesthood" in Christ?
- Can I honestly say, "You are my portion, Lord"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You called the Levites to serve You, and their inheritance was You Yourself. Help me to treasure Your nearness above every earthly portion. Thank You that in Christ I am set apart to serve You. Be my inheritance and my greatest reward. Amen.
